title: The written rules say to settle a request for a system look with one filmed card, not five builds
goal: On 2026-09-29 and 30 the loop built the segmented control five ways in two days: drawn, painted glass, the Mac's own, then our drawn one again with a glass chip after the user called the Mac's own ugly. The design rules should say that when a request names a system look (Liquid Glass, the Mac's own control), the runner films the system's version beside ours and asks once on a card before building a second variant. The loop's own notes should also agree on how often the whole walk set runs.
notes: Filed by the 2026-09-30 digest's design review. Evidence: done tasks the-segmented-control-s-thumb-is-lighter-than-it, the-segmented-thumb-glides-like-a-mac-control-no, try-the-segmented-thumb-on-the-system-s-own-liqu, every-segmented-control-is-the-one-system-glass, then every-segmented-control-is-apple-s-own-liquid-gl deleting them all; dropped the-picked-segment-s-label-is-readable-on-the-gl and the-segmented-thumb-moves-the-way-the-user-likes; commits 605a5c4a through 5a81d5a3. The digest already fixed the same twelve-hours wording in queue/bin/runner-prompt.md and queue/bin/digest-prompt.md (the code, queue/bin/sweep-schedule.mjs, says 24 hours); CLAUDE.md line 38 is the one left, outside the digest's reach.
acceptance: UX-PATTERNS.md has one short rule near the placement contract: a request that names a system look or material gets one card with the system's version filmed beside ours before a second build, citing the segmented control as the example, including the user's 2026-09-30 call to keep our drawn control with a tinted glass chip
The rule does NOT say the system control always wins: the user sent the Mac's own segmented control back on 2026-09-30, so the drawn control stays
queue/bin/runner-prompt.md and queue/bin/manager-prompt.md point at that rule where they tell a runner how to build a control

CLAUDE.md's build and test table says the full walk set runs at most once every twenty four hours (queue/bin/sweep.sh schedule), not twice a day, and its walk count and length are the current ones or are left out

log.note: triage 2026-10-01: rewritten. The first version asked for a rule that the Mac's own control comes first, but the user sent the Mac's own segmented control back on 2026-09-30 ("this IS the native slider, but it's ugly and I want to go back to our custom one"), so that rule would contradict them. The lesson kept is the cost: five builds where one filmed card would have asked the question.
